scope: Worker nf_tables batch publication through the original shared rules transaction; live policy for existing native TCP capabilities, retained original shared socket lifetime and canonical SO_ERROR completion. Remove the Netlink owner-admission checkpoint.
method: Four independent processes, four Trames vCPUs. Publication/query/pipe use 1,000 iterations and three counterbalanced unprofiled repeats; ordinary TCP scalar/vector/message controls use 10,000 iterations and nine counterbalanced unprofiled repeats. Each group has a separate diagnostic repeat. Publication sends one NFNL batch creating and deleting the process-specific table, then validates its 36-byte success ACK and sequence. Setup/cleanup is outside the loop. Native ARM Linux runs the identical static musl ELF on six vCPUs; publication requires NET_ADMIN and runs as root only inside the isolated local CI machine. All final builds and affected CI/FFI finish before measurement. Linux is stopped before Mac measurements. Native macOS uses its original APIs for TCP/pipe; there is no native Netlink substitute.
comparison_limits: Publication measures bounded create/delete transactions with no live hook; functional live DROP/counter/receive/completion behavior is separately tested. Native Linux implements full nf_tables semantics and uses process-specific names with different PID lengths; these are contextual results, not proof of generally faster-than-native operation. Query responses remain 292 bytes in Trames versus 1,488 in Linux. TCP controls show no observed degradation; no control gain or statistical regression bound is claimed. No whole-app, Firefox or physical-iPad performance claim.

implementation.shared_rules: Existing per-firewall RwLock transaction, staging, validation, generation, response capacity and shared counters. Successful commit updates actual rules and relaxed atomic empty-hook selector together under that writer; failure updates neither.
implementation.live_policy: Immutable policy attachment before shared socket publication points to original namespace and actual firewall object. Each native byte attempt selects original full packet evaluation only when hooks exist. Empty-policy calls avoid namespace/rules locks and do not cache an allow across waits.
implementation.ownership: DirectTcp/DirectControl/TcpPoll use one weak original-socket pointer. Accepted TcpLease retains that complete shared native socket, preserving original policy after close/reuse. Capability sizes and per-admission reference-count operation counts stay unchanged; no new wrapper allocation.
implementation.completion: SO_ERROR delegates to original shared socket completion and error consumption, eliminating cached unfiltered completion admission.
implementation.waiting: Existing host registry owns the same type-erased Arc and drops the final resource outside its registry lock. Poll/capability snapshots stay weak. Existing conditional-close check observes socket and transport leases.
implementation.removed_dependency: Delete worker_send_supported/Prepared.worker_admitted and per-message owner/deferred state for nf_tables; all Netlink data/batches share worker progress.
implementation.synchronization: No new global algorithm lock, coordinator/service thread, polling bus, ordinary guest-memory fence, unsafe code or native-only access policy. Actual filtering retains its original locks and transactions.
